t.5.60.1: Hanūmān, the best of the monkeys, a bull among the vānaras, said to them: "O vānaras, with untroubled minds, enjoy the honey!"
t.5.60.2: Having heard Hanumān's words, Aṅgada, foremost of the monkeys, replied with a gladdened heart: "Let the monkeys drink the honey."
t.5.60.4: Having heard these words from the mouth of Aṅgada, the bull-like monkeys, the foremost among the vānaras, were delighted and honoured them, crying, "Well said, well said!"
t.5.60.3: The word of Hanumān, who has accomplished his task, must certainly be carried out by me; even what ought not to be done must be done, so how much more something such as this?
t.5.60.5: Having honored Aṅgada, the bull among monkeys, all the monkeys went swiftly to Madhuvana, like the rushing current of a river.
t.5.60.7: Then all of them, leaping up and gathering together, beat by the hundreds the forest-guards who were clinging to them in the Madhuvana.
t.5.60.6: Overjoyed at having seen Maithilī and heard news of her, those bold ones, emboldened by the leave they had been given, forcibly overran the Madhuvana and its guards.
t.5.60.8: Seizing in their arms honeycombs as large as a droṇa measure, they all together smashed them, and likewise in another spot they devoured them.
t.5.60.9: Some honey-tawny monkeys, having drunk the honey, fling away the rest, and some, wild with frenzy, struck one another with beeswax.
t.5.60.10: Others, at the foot of the trees, one of them standing there clutching a branch, utterly exhausted with intoxication, spread out leaves and lie down to sleep.
t.5.60.12: The monkeys, intoxicated with honey, behaved variously: some let out roars, some warbled as if in delight, and some lay asleep on the surface of the earth.
t.5.60.11: The monkeys, as though gone mad and drunk with honey, joyfully hurl things at one another, while others likewise stumble and reel about.
t.5.60.13: And even those who were the honey-guardians here, the servants of Dadhimukha, were driven back by those fearsome monkeys and fled in all directions.
t.5.60.14: Dragged along by their knees and shown the path of the gods, the guards, deeply distressed, went to Dadhimukha and spoke these words.
t.5.60.16: Then the monkey Dadhimukha, guardian of the grove there, enraged on hearing that the Madhuvana had been ravaged, tried to placate those monkeys.
t.5.60.15: The Madhuvana has been destroyed by force by those to whom Hanūmān granted leave, and we were dragged by our knees and shown the path of the gods.
t.5.60.17: Come, come here! Let us go; by force we shall restrain those monkeys, swollen with arrogance, who are devouring the honey.
t.5.60.18: Having heard these words of Dadhimukha, the heroic bulls among the monkeys went back to Madhuvana together with him.
t.5.60.19: And in their midst Dadhimukha, seizing a very great tree, rushed forward with speed, and so did all those monkeys.
t.5.60.20: Those monkeys, enraged, seized rocks, trees and stones as well, and rushed to the place where those elephants among monkeys were.
t.5.60.21: Fixing that command of their master firmly in their hearts, those heroes, armed with sāla trees, palm trees and rocks, rushed forward in haste.
t.5.60.22: There those heroic guardians, in their thousands, advanced upon the monkeys, puffed up with pride in their strength, both those in the trees and those on the ground.
t.5.60.23: Then, seeing Dadhimukha enraged, the bulls among monkeys, led by Hanūmān, rushed at him with great speed.
t.5.60.24: As that mighty-armed and immensely powerful elder came rushing at him, tree in hand, the enraged Aṅgada struck his venerable kinsman there with both arms.
t.5.60.25: Blinded by intoxication, he did not recognize him, did not think, "This is my venerable elder," and he swiftly and violently crushed him against the surface of the earth.
t.5.60.26: That heroic elephant among monkeys, his arms broken, turned away, shaken and drenched in blood, suddenly fell into a swoon for a moment.
t.5.60.27: That bull among monkeys, having somehow been set free by those monkeys, went to a secluded place and spoke to those servants who had gathered there.
t.5.60.28: Let these remain here; we go to where our master, the broad-necked monkey Sugrīva, stays together with Rāma.
t.5.60.29: I shall make known to the king the whole of the wrong committed by Aṅgada; on hearing my words, the wrathful one will have the monkeys put to death.
t.5.60.30: For this Madhuvana is beloved of the great-souled Sugrīva; it is a divine grove inherited from his father and grandfather, hard to approach even for the gods.
t.5.60.31: Sugrīva will have all these monkeys, greedy for honey, put to death by punishment, together with their friends and kinsmen, for their lives are already forfeit.
t.5.60.32: These evil-minded ones, who scorn the king's command, must surely be slain; our anger, born of indignation, will bear fruit.
t.5.60.33: Having spoken thus to the forest-guards, the mighty Dadhimukha swiftly leapt up into the air and departed, accompanied by the forest-guards.
t.5.60.34: In the mere space of a twinkling, that forest-dweller reached the place where the wise monkey Sugrīva, son of the thousand-rayed sun, was.
t.5.60.35: Having seen Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva too, he dropped down from the sky onto the level ground of the earth.
t.5.60.36: Swooping down, the mighty monkey Dadhimukha, supreme lord of the guards, surrounded by all those guards, rushed upon them.
t.5.60.37: He, his face downcast, joined his palms in reverence upon his head and pressed his own head against the auspicious feet of Sugrīva.
